NDT training in Minneapolis: how it works for Minneapolis employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET to employers and technicians across Minneapolis-St. Paul, with live online classroom sessions and hands-on practical sessions onsite at your facility. Your employer certifies you under its written practice once you complete training, documented experience, Level III-administered general, specific and practical exams and a vision test.

The Twin Cities NDT market is unusually broad. Within an hour of downtown Minneapolis you have two refineries south and east of St. Paul, two nuclear stations on the Mississippi, a major airline maintenance base at MSP, aerospace and defence manufacturers, medical device makers, food and agricultural processing plants, and a large network of fabricators and machine shops. Add pipeline operators crossing the state and the Minnesota Department of Transportation's steel bridge inventory, and a Twin Cities technician could spend a career in almost any NDT sector without moving.

That variety is why the employer-based SNT-TC-1A model matters. Each employer's written practice defines what its technicians need, and each sector adds its own layer. Atlantis NDT does not run a training centre in Minneapolis; theory is taught live online, and practical sessions are delivered onsite at the employer's facility on its own equipment under ASNT Level III oversight. Request a Minneapolis training quote with your methods, levels and head-count.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Minneapolis

Each course follows the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge. Level I covers performing calibrations and tests to written instructions under supervision; Level II covers setting up and calibrating equipment, interpreting and evaluating results against codes and specifications, and reporting; Level III preparation covers the basic, method and specific examinations. Recommended hours of training and experience are in SNT-TC-1A and are adopted by your written practice; the training requirements matrix is our reference.

MethodLevelsWhat Minneapolis employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic testing)I, II, III prepCorrosion and thickness surveys at refineries, weld inspection on pressure equipment and bridges, bond inspection on composite and aerospace partsBasic maths; Level II requires Level I training and experience
PAUT (phased array UT)II, III prepCorrosion mapping on refinery piping and vessels, weld inspection on turnaround repairs and pipelinesUT Level II normally required first
TOFD (time-of-flight diffraction)II, III prepThick-wall pressure vessel welds and in-service crack sizing supportUT Level II normally required first
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, III prepRefinery and pipeline weld radiography, casting and component inspection, digital radiography in manufacturingRadiation safety training plus Minnesota requirements below
MT (magnetic particle testing)I, II, III prepStructural welds on steel bridges, rotating equipment and shafts, mining equipment components, landing-gear partsNone beyond employer requirements
PT (liquid penetrant testing)I, II, III prepAerospace components, stainless food-grade and pharmaceutical piping, turbine and valve partsNone beyond employer requirements
VT (visual testing)I, II, III prepWeld visual on fabrication and construction, in-service visual on bridges and plant equipmentNone beyond employer requirements
ET (eddy current testing)I, II, III prepAircraft structure and wheel inspection, heat-exchanger and condenser tubing at refineries and power plantsBasic electrical theory helpful

How the methods map to Twin Cities work. Refinery and petrochemical work in Dakota and Washington counties uses UT thickness and PAUT corrosion mapping in the run-up to and during turnarounds, RT on repair welds, and ET on exchanger bundles. Airline maintenance at MSP and the region's aerospace manufacturers use ET, PT and MT heavily, often under manufacturer procedures and customer schemes such as NAS 410, which Atlantis does not train to but which build on the same method knowledge. Bridge fabrication and inspection draws on UT, MT and VT under AWS D1.5 and owner requirements. Food-grade and medical manufacturing, which the Twin Cities has in depth, relies on PT and VT for stainless welds and components.

New technicians commonly start with PT and MT, add UT, and then specialise in PAUT, RT or ET depending on sector. See the full course list on the NDT training page, and ASNT Level III preparation for experienced Level IIs.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Minneapolis, step by step

  1. Confirm the written practice. SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice; the employer's written practice makes it binding and sets the levels, training, experience, exam and recertification rules.
  2. Complete formal classroom training. Theory, equipment, techniques, codes and interpretation, delivered live online or in an onsite session. The training requirements matrix lists recommended hours.
  3. Log on-the-job experience. Supervised hours performing the method, recorded in a format your Level III accepts. Turnaround work at the refineries can build experience quickly; make sure every shift is logged.
  4. Pass the general examination. Written questions on method principles, administered under the authority of a Level III.
  5. Pass the specific examination. Written questions on your employer's procedures, equipment and codes, such as ASME Section V and B31.3 for refinery piping, AWS D1.5 for bridges, or manufacturer manuals for aircraft.
  6. Pass the practical examination. Hands-on testing of specimens with known discontinuities, graded by the Level III.
  7. Pass the vision tests. Near-vision acuity annually and colour contrast differentiation.
  8. Receive written certification from the employer for each method and level.
  9. Recertify at the interval in the written practice. A new employer must recertify you under its own written practice.

More: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Minneapolis crews

Live online theory. Classroom modules are taught live by an instructor over video. Technicians in Minneapolis, St. Paul, Bloomington, Rosemount, Cottage Grove or out-state Minnesota join without driving across the metro in winter. See online NDT training.

Onsite practical at your facility. Practical sessions run at the employer's site, on its own instruments and specimens, under ASNT Level III oversight. A refinery contractor trains on piping and vessel specimens that match its work; a manufacturer trains on its own parts and reference standards.

Scheduling around turnarounds, outages and winter. Refineries and power plants in Minnesota generally schedule major maintenance outside the coldest months, and contractors ramp up hiring beforehand. Training in the months before a spring or fall turnaround means new technicians are certified and ready when the work starts. Minnesota winters also affect outdoor practical work: penetrant testing has a standard temperature range in ASME Section V, and couplant and equipment behave differently on frozen steel, so outdoor sessions are planned for warmer periods or indoor bays. Ask about onsite training for your Minneapolis crew; cohort and onsite quotes are usually returned within one business day.

Corporate programmes. Employers training several technicians can combine theory, practical sessions, exams and written-practice support through corporate NDT training.

Where NDT technicians work in Minneapolis

Refining and petrochemicals. The Pine Bend refinery in Rosemount and the St. Paul Park refinery supply much of the upper Midwest with fuels. In-service inspection is driven by owner programmes built on API inspection codes, with ASME Section V governing NDT methods and ASME B31.3 and Section VIII applying to piping and vessels. Contractors supporting these sites need UT, PAUT, RT, MT, PT and ET technicians, especially during turnarounds. Atlantis does not provide API 510 or 570 inspector training, but SNT-TC-1A method training is the NDT foundation for those roles.

Nuclear and fossil power. Xcel Energy operates the Prairie Island nuclear plant near Red Wing and the Monticello nuclear plant northwest of the metro, along with gas and coal generation. Outage inspection covers piping, valves, steam generator and condenser tubing, and structural welds, under ASME Section XI-based owner programmes with additional utility qualification requirements.

Aviation maintenance and aerospace. MSP hosts a large airline maintenance operation, and the Twin Cities has aerospace and defence manufacturers and suppliers. ET, PT and MT dominate, typically under manufacturer procedures and customer qualification schemes.

Pipelines. Major crude and gas pipelines cross Minnesota, including the Enbridge mainline system through the north of the state. Construction and integrity work uses RT and PAUT to API 1104, UT for integrity digs, and falls under federal PHMSA rules with Minnesota's Office of Pipeline Safety overseeing intrastate lines.

Bridges and infrastructure. After the 2007 collapse of the I-35W Mississippi River bridge in Minneapolis, steel bridge inspection gained a very high profile in Minnesota. MnDOT and local agencies inspect steel bridges, including fracture-critical members, using VT, MT and UT, and new steel bridges are fabricated to AWS D1.5.

Manufacturing, medical devices and food processing. Precision manufacturers, medical device makers and food and agricultural processors across the metro use PT and VT on stainless welds, UT and RT on castings and components, and ET for material and surface checks. Mining equipment suppliers serving the Iron Range add MT and UT on heavy welded structures.

Radiography licensing in Minnesota. Minnesota is an NRC Agreement State. The Minnesota Department of Health licenses radioactive material, including industrial radiography sources, under Minnesota Rules chapter 4731, and registers X-ray equipment separately. Radiographers must meet state radiation-safety training and certification requirements, and field radiography at temporary job sites requires at least two qualified individuals. These requirements are separate from SNT-TC-1A method certification. Confirm current rules with the Department of Health before planning RT work.

Level III services and written practices for Minneapolis NDT companies

Twin Cities inspection contractors often need to satisfy several owner audits at once, while manufacturers need a written practice that fits customer quality requirements. Atlantis supports both with:

  • Written practice development and revision. See written practice development.
  • Outside Level III services: exam preparation, administration and grading, procedure review and records.
  • Procedures and technique sheets for UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, referencing ASME, AWS and customer specifications.
  • Pre-turnaround and pre-audit records checks so certifications, experience logs and vision tests are complete before owner prequalification.
  • SNT-TC-1A guidance for managers. See SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Book a Level III consultation for your Twin Cities operation.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. Twin Cities technicians heading into refinery work can use the oil and gas site and storage tank environments; aviation technicians can use the aircraft hangar.

It is practice only. It helps you rehearse set-ups and interpretation, but it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens and is not on-the-job experience.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, examinations and Level III services, and supervises onsite practical delivery.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Minneapolis

How do I get NDT certified in Minneapolis?

Work for, or be hired by, an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice. Complete classroom training, log supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and pass the vision tests. The employer issues your certification.

Can I take NDT training online in Minnesota?

Yes. Theory is delivered live online across Minnesota where the written practice accepts it; practical training is hands-on and runs onsite at the employer's facility. See online NDT training.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your written practice and your UT Level I record. SNT-TC-1A recommended hours are shown in the training requirements matrix; experience usually takes longest.

Do I need a license for radiography in Minnesota?

The employer needs a Minnesota Department of Health licence for radioactive sources, or registration for X-ray equipment, and radiographers must meet state certification and radiation-safety requirements. SNT-TC-1A RT certification is separate. Confirm current requirements with the Department.

What does NDT training cost in Minneapolis?

Quote on request, depending on method, level, group size, onsite practical needs and any exam or written-practice work. Request a Minneapolis training quote; replies usually come within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Twin Cities employers?

Yes, SNT-TC-1A-based certification is the standard framework for industrial NDT in Minnesota. Refinery employers may also want API inspector credentials, and aerospace employers NAS 410; Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only.

Which method is most useful for refinery turnaround work?

UT thickness and PAUT corrosion mapping are in heavy demand, with RT, MT, PT and ET also used. UT Level II is a strong starting point.

Can NDT be done outdoors in a Minnesota winter?

Yes, with care. Penetrant testing below the ASME Section V standard temperature range needs a qualified procedure, and UT couplant and equipment need cold-weather planning. The course covers these limits.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Minneapolis?

No. Theory is live online and practical sessions run onsite at the employer's facility.

Can Atlantis provide Level III services to a Twin Cities contractor?

Yes, for SNT-TC-1A programmes: written practices, exams, procedures and audit preparation.

How do I prepare for ASNT Level III from Minneapolis?

Level III preparation runs live online, and practice material such as UT Level 2 practice questions is available.

What do NDT technicians earn in Minnesota?

Pay depends on method, level, sector and travel. See the NDT salary guide.
